transcript:
Header: Date: 2025-06-11 | Time: 09:00 PT | Duration: 45m
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Diego Morales (Redwood SE), Priya Ramesh (Redwood Partner Ops); Maya Chen (AstraNova Partnerships), Omar Ruiz (AstraNova Partner Sales), Danielle Park (Solutions), Tom Hsu (AstraNova AE)

Summary: quick pipeline review and deal strategy; align on who owns intros, technical gating items, and next steps for three priority opportunities. Discussed risk areas (latency/cost, data residency for EU accounts, SOC2/compliance asks) and proposed playbook items.

Topics: pipeline health, technical blockers, joint GTM motions, next steps and owners

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Lena Park: Hey everyone, thanks for making time; super excited to catch up on the co-sell pipeline. Maya, Omar, you good if we jump in?
[00:07] Maya Chen: Yup, good here, thanks Lena.
[00:10] Omar Ruiz: All set. Quick note we have Tom and Danielle to cover some solution details.
[00:16] Lena Park: Great. Diego, do you want to kick with a quick recap of Redwood bits relevant to deals?
[00:21] Diego Morales: Yeah for sure. Quick context - Redwood offers hosted API, Dedicated reserved capacity, and Private VPC/on-prem options. For most partner-led deals we see tradeoffs: hosted is fastest, dedicated for predictable throughput, and private for regulated customers. We also have Redwood Console for observability and Redwood Optimize for batching/quantization guidance. Wanted to highlight KV cache and prefix caching which reduce token cost for chat-heavy flows, that usually helps procurement.
[00:40] Danielle Park: Sorry, small interruption - when you say Dedicated are you talking about physical GPU pools we provision or is that still multi-tenant?
[00:47] Diego Morales: Good question. Dedicated is logically isolated and we allocate reserved GPU pools, so it's not multi-tenant in the sense of shared capacity. There are options for burst capacity onto host pools but base is reserved to the customer.
[00:58] Tom Hsu: Any ballpark numbers for latency p50/p95? Our customers ask that a lot.
[01:04] Diego Morales: Ballpark depends on model; for a 32k context Llama-like variant on A100 class, p50 around 100-140ms per token, p95 tends to be higher - 600-900ms depending on sequence length. We can run quick checks on the exact model and prompt shape for each deal.
[01:20] Lena Park: Cool, we flagged three priority opps in the spreadsheet: Deal A (US SaaS, low latency requirement), Deal B (EU regulated bank, data residency + SOC2), Deal C (mid-market retail with cost sensitivity). Maya, can you confirm AstraNova's view of priorities?
[01:33] Maya Chen: Yes ranking aligns: Deal A and B are top. Deal B is particularly strategic - they have strict data residency and need an on-prem or VPC solution.
[01:43] Omar Ruiz: On Deal A we already have a 1:1 with the customer's platform lead, need Redwood on a technical call to lock perf numbers.
[01:50] Lena Park: Diego is your SE to run that. Diego: can you scope a quick perf checklist and validate batching / kv cache benefits?
[01:57] Diego Morales: Yep I'll run p50/p95, check batching settings, whether we can enable prefix caching and estimated cost delta. Should be able to share a one-pager by 2025-06-18.
[02:06] Maya Chen: For Deal B, compliance will be the gating factor. They asked for SOC2 and customer-managed KMS and audit logs. Does Redwood support that for Private?
[02:16] Priya Ramesh: Yes, for Private we support customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations, audit logs, and can run in VPC or fully on-prem in our enterprise package. SOC 2 report is available, we can share the cert and SOC2 documentation.
[02:29] Tom Hsu: Perfect. Any long lead times for on-prem installs?
[02:33] Priya Ramesh: On-prem tends to be multi-week depending on infra readiness, but we have packages to accelerate; we also often recommend VPC deployment first for speed and then on-prem if they require air-gap.
[02:44] Omar Ruiz: Good to know. For Deal C the ask is cost - they're comparing to self-hosting and other APIs. Any playbook items we should use?
[02:52] Lena Park: Yes, Diego and Redwood Optimize can produce a cost vs perf recommendation: quantization levels, batching, and cache settings. Also share unit economics per 1M tokens.
[03:01] Diego Morales: We'll include recommended model variants (e.g., 7B quantized vs 13B) and expected latency/cost tradeoffs.
[03:07] Maya Chen: On co-sell motions - AstraNova can run joint outreach to top 20 accounts. We prefer joint email + intro call then technical deep-dive with Redwood SE. Any materials you want us to use?
[03:18] Lena Park: We'll provide a joint deck and a short 1-pager playbook. I'll drop the deck link in the pipeline spreadsheet.
[03:24] Omar Ruiz: Can you also include a short tech FAQ for Deal A - common gating Qs for platform teams?
[03:29] Diego Morales: I'll add an FAQ covering p50/p95 numbers, KV cache, quantization, and SSO/SAML options.
[03:36] Maya Chen: A couple of risk flags: for EU deals the customer asked about data residency and whether logs leave region. Is that a showstopper?
[03:43] Priya Ramesh: We support region-specific private deployments and can configure audit logging to remain in-region. For hosted we also offer region-limited routing but for strict residency we recommend Dedicated or Private.
[03:54] Danielle Park: On the procurement side, how do contracts usually look for partner-driven deals? Any standard reseller addendum?
[04:01] Lena Park: We have partner reseller terms and co-sell SOW templates. Priya can share redacted examples. Typically there's a rev-share split and some joint commit for inbound leads depending on program level.
[04:12] Priya Ramesh: I'll share the partner program doc and a sample rev-share framework after this call.
[04:17] Tom Hsu: For the technical deep-dive calls, who should we route to? Diego is fine but sometimes customers want a longer performance bench with model-specific kernels.
[04:26] Diego Morales: For deeper kernel-level perf we can loop in our infra team; for initial scoping I'm the right person. If they need hardware-level tuning we escalate.
[04:33] Maya Chen: Great. For Deal A timeline: customer wants a decision by end of quarter (mid-July). We need a technical session within two weeks.
[04:41] Lena Park: Okay I'll set that up. Proposed: Redwood + AstraNova joint technical call with customer's platform lead next week. I'll send invite.
[04:46] Omar Ruiz: Also flagged potential competitor motion - customer evaluating Vertex and Cohere; price is sensitive. We should emphasize predictable latency and our dedicated offering.
[04:55] Lena Park: Agree - our pitch will focus on predictable SLOs, caching to reduce cost, and ability to fall back to smaller model variants.
[05:02] Danielle Park: Quick question on demo artifacts - any sample benchmarks or case studies we can include in outreach?
[05:07] Lena Park: Yes, I'll attach a short benchmark sheet and a case study PDF showing latency and cost wins for a similar SaaS customer.
[05:14] Maya Chen: For co-sell attribution, what's the process to log deals so AstraNova gets credit?
[05:19] Priya Ramesh: Use the partner pipeline spreadsheet and tag deals with partner account IDs; we'll handle CRM attribution and send monthly reports.
[05:26] Omar Ruiz: One nit - some customers are worried about throttling and rate limits on hosted. Can you clarify throttling guarantees?
[05:33] Diego Morales: Hosted has rate limits and quotas per API key; Dedicated provides guaranteed throughput with SLA-backed targets. We'll include recommended rate-limit settings and quota commitments per offering in the deck.
[05:44] Tom Hsu: On the SOC2 docs - can you send the attestation and any penetration test summaries?
[05:49] Priya Ramesh: Yes will share SOC2, ISO certs, and a high-level summary of recent pentesting.
[05:56] Maya Chen: For Deal B the bank will want an on-site audit possibly. Is Redwood open to that?
[06:01] Priya Ramesh: Yes we can accommodate formal audits for enterprise customers; we'll coordinate via our security team.
[06:07] Lena Park: Ok wrapping to next steps: I'll share the joint spreadsheet and deck, Diego will run perf checklist for Deal A, Priya will share partner docs + SOC2, Maya to confirm intros. Anything else?
[06:18] Omar Ruiz: Can we also line up a short exec-level sync if Deal B goes to procurement? A VP level intro would help.
[06:24] Lena Park: Absolutely - we'll block time w/c 2025-06-23 for exec intro if needed.
[06:29] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone. One more thing - for outreach cadence, AstraNova prefers two-touch: email then LinkedIn. We'll coordinate.
[06:34] Lena Park: Perfect. I'll send notes and action items. Thanks all.
[06:38] Diego Morales: Thanks, bye.
[06:40] Meeting ended
